messages.content: Hi Liu. I'm Hua. I've been planning a trip to Tibet for ages, since last winter. I really want to take the high-speed rail from Beijing to Lhasa, but I'm worried about the altitude. Do you think it's safe for a young person like me?

Hello Hua! Of course it's safe if you prepare well. Many young travelers have taken that route successfully. Actually, the train has special oxygen equipment, and staff check your condition regularly. Have you thought about booking your ticket in advance? Prices can go up quickly during spring festivals.

Yes, I have checked the prices. But the scenery is amazing too! I heard there are stops near Qinghai Lake and Hoh Xil. Maybe I should stop there for a day to see the yaks and take some photos before continuing.

That sounds wonderful! Qinghai Lake is breathtaking in spring, especially when the ice melts. You could definitely plan a short stop. But have you considered how the altitude might affect you during the journey itself? It gets higher as you go west.

I guess so. Anyway, speaking of beautiful places, have you ever been to the Grand Bazaar in Kashgar? It's a completely different setting from the train, with colorful carpets, spicy lamb skewers, and loud music everywhere. I think I'd love to visit there next time instead of going to Tibet.

Well, Kashgar is indeed very lively and has great food! But let's get back to your Tibet trip for now. Speaking of preparations, what kind of clothes do you plan to pack for the high-altitude stations?
Oh, thanks for asking. I will pack a warm down jacket and some wool socks. Also, maybe some red dates and ginger tea to keep my energy up while on the train.

That's a smart idea. Red dates and ginger tea are perfect for warming up your body in the cold air at high altitude. I think you're making good plans overall. Are you still considering the train or maybe flying part of the way?
I prefer the train because it's slower, which means my body can adjust gradually. Flying feels too sudden for such a big change in height. What about the other passengers? Are there many families?

Yes, there are quite a few families, especially during holidays. Many parents bring children to see the mountains and lakes. By the way, do you know if there are any dining cars where you can eat local Tibetan food during the trip?
Yes, I heard there is a dining car with butter tea and tsampa. It sounds delicious, although I'm not used to that taste. Maybe I should try it once I get used to the environment.

It's definitely worth a try! Butter tea has a unique flavor that many people enjoy after a while. If you're worried about the taste, you can bring some bottled drinks from Xi'an just in case. Have you decided when exactly you want to travel this year?
I plan to go in May. It's not too crowded yet, and the weather should be nice. I hope the train runs on time and I don't get any altitude sickness. Thank you, Liu!

May is a great choice, Hua. Just remember to drink plenty of water and avoid heavy meals right before the trip. I'm sure your journey will be smooth and full of wonderful memories. Let me know if you need help with booking details!

messages.content: Hello Lao Zhang! I'm Jing Hua from Hangzhou. I want to buy some Dragonwell tea leaves as a gift for my friends back in Ningbo. Do you have any good recommendations?

Hello Jing Hua! Yes, I have the best Longjing tea here. Since I've been selling it on this Old Street for twenty years, I know exactly which batches are fresh. For a gift, you should get the spring harvest ones; they are a bit more expensive but very special.
That sounds perfect. Usually, I buy tea online, but I prefer buying here because I can see the leaves and talk to the seller. How much is it per jin? I think fifty yuan is a fair price.

Well, actually, our price is eighty yuan for one jin. But don't worry, we can negotiate. If you buy two jin, I can give you a discount. You know, quality is very important when you send gifts to family.

Oh, I see. Okay, let's say I buy two jin then. But actually, Lao Zhang, I have a question about your life. How old are you exactly, and when did you first open this shop? Do you have any children or grandchildren living nearby in the Old Street?

Ah, you know a lot about me! I'm sixty-five years old, and I opened this shop in 2004. My son lives in Xihu District, so he helps me sometimes with the accounting. Anyway, let's talk about the tea instead. Shall I wrap these two jin of Longjing in a nice box for your friends?
Yes, please wrap it nicely. I also want to buy some roasted tea next time. Do you sell Pu'er tea? I've heard it gets better with age, just like wine.

Yes, we have Pu'er tea from Yunnan. Although it's different from Longjing, it's also very popular. Many people in Chengdu and Guiyang love to drink it. We can make a small cake for you if you want to try it later.
Great idea. I'll take the Longjing now. By the way, what time does the market close today? I want to walk around the street to see the other souvenirs before I go home.

The market usually closes at six PM. But since it's spring, many vendors stay until seven. You should go to the side street near the bridge; there are nice silk scarves there. Would you like me to call a taxi for you after we finish?
That would be very kind of you. Thank you, Lao Zhang. I feel very happy to meet such a friendly vendor today.
It's my pleasure, Jing Hua! You are always welcome here. Now, let me wrap this tea for you. It's ready soon!

messages.content: Hello, Lao Zhang! I'm Jing Hua. I'm looking for some good tea leaves to send to my family back in Hangzhou.
Hello, Jing Hua! Welcome to my shop. We have many kinds of tea here, like Longjing and Biluochun. Which one do you prefer?
I think Longjing is famous, but Biluochun smells nice too. Do you have any special gifts for packaging?
Yes, of course! We can put the tea in a nice bamboo box or a red silk bag. It's perfect for giving to friends. What do you think?
Actually, I've been thinking a lot lately about how modern life is changing everything. Do you feel that young people today lose the connection to nature that older generations had?
Well, that's an interesting thought. I guess many young people are busy with work and school. Anyway, speaking of tea, how much would you like to buy today?
Maybe two packs of Longjing. Can we try a small amount first before I decide on the full box?
That's a good idea. Let me take a small jar for you to taste. It's not expensive, and you can choose the best quality.
Okay, let's do that. But I have to ask, is it true that tea shops like this one are disappearing in big cities like Shanghai?
Actually, no! There are still many small shops like mine. In fact, more people are coming back to try traditional tea. Would you like to sit down and have a cup now?
Yes, please! I'd love to taste it. How much is the small jar, and can I pay with my phone?
It's only 30 yuan. Yes, you can pay with your phone. We accept Alipay and WeChat Pay. Would you like to add some Biluochun as a gift for your friend too?

messages.content: Hi, I'm Lin. It's really hot tonight at the night market in Guilin. Have you tried the grilled squid yet? I heard the sauce is amazing.
Hello Lin! Yes, I've had some already. It's delicious, especially if you add the chili oil. The prices here are quite reasonable for students, aren't they?
I agree. By the way, I went to the new art museum in Suzhou last weekend. The exhibition about ancient paintings was really impressive.

Wow, that sounds interesting! Well, I actually prefer street food like this. Anyway, have you found any good restaurants in Nanning that serve cheap rice noodles since you are looking for affordable meals?
Oh, I forgot to mention something else. I'm thinking of moving to Yantai next month because the weather there is much better.

That's a big decision! To be honest, I guess you should check the rent prices in Yantai first. Speaking of food, I think the beef noodles in Chongqing are a bit spicy, but very tasty. Have you ever eaten them?
No, I haven't. They sound too hot for me. What do you think about the dumplings in Xi'an? My friend says they are the best.

Actually, I've tried them before. They are indeed famous, although the vinegar dipping sauce is key. Did you know there is a specific type of dumpling called 'yangchun' that is very popular in Guizhou?
Yes, I know a little about that. But I'm more interested in the soup today. Is the chicken porridge here good?
Yes! The chicken porridge in Guangxi is famous for being soft and fragrant. It's a great choice if you want something warm and not too spicy. Have you ordered it yet?
Not yet. I'm waiting for my friend to join me. Do you usually come here alone?
Usually, I come with my roommate or alone. Actually, I like the quiet atmosphere sometimes. If you don't mind, would you like some ginger water after your meal?
That sounds nice. I will take one. Thank you for the advice.

Oh, that sounds amazing! I've heard about it but I'm a bit worried about the price. Are the portions big enough for a student budget?

Wait, you want to visit the Great Wall in Chongqing? That's impossible, isn't it? The Great Wall is in Beijing, not Chongqing.

That's true. But I still think I should go to Beijing to see the Great Wall. It's my dream destination.

messages.content: Hello! I'm Wei. It's really misty here near Mount Qingcheng this morning. The humidity is so high, I feel like I'm in a cloud. Have you lived here all your life?

Hi Wei! Yes, I've lived in this village since I was a child. The mist is beautiful, isn't it? Actually, it happens every rainy season. I used to hate it because I couldn't see the path clearly, but now I love it. What about you? Do you like hiking here?
Yes, I do. But this rain is making it hard to plan. Maybe we can hike after the storm stops? I really want to see the peaks.
That's a good idea. If the rain stops by noon, we can go up to the Jade Peak. It's not very far from our village. I think the view will be amazing once the clouds clear.

Speaking of your home, do you have any family members still living here? I'm wondering if you have siblings or cousins who might know more about the old traditions in this area. Maybe you could tell me about your childhood memories growing up in a family like yours?

Oh, yes! Well, I have an older brother who lives in Chengdu now, and my younger sister stayed here. To be honest, my childhood was very happy because my family always cooked delicious hotpot together. Anyway, let's talk about the hiking plan. If we go tomorrow, what time should we start?
Okay, let's say 9 AM. I will bring my camera. Do you think the trail will be muddy?
Yes, it might be muddy because the ground is wet. You should wear good hiking shoes. In addition, there are many bamboo forests on the way, so it will be very green and cool.
That sounds perfect. I haven't hiked in bamboo forests before. Is there a specific spot you recommend for taking photos?

Definitely! There is a small waterfall near the entrance of the forest. The mist makes the water look very special. Also, you can see some old temples there. Have you ever visited any temples in your hometown?
No, I haven't. I usually stay in the city. I guess I should try to experience more nature soon.
That's a great decision! Actually, nature is very relaxing. By the way, after the hike, we can have some fresh tea and local snacks. What kind of tea do you like?

I agree. When the rain stops, I plan to hike up to the old temple. Do you know the way?

That sounds nice. But honestly, sometimes I feel like modern people are too busy to stop and appreciate nature. They should slow down and think about what really matters in life, instead of just chasing money all the time.

Yes, sure. I love spicy food. What kind of noodles are popular here in this village?
Well, we usually eat Dan Dan noodles here. It has minced beef and lots of chili oil. It is very delicious and perfect after a hike.
That sounds amazing. I haven't tried Dan Dan noodles before. Let's go get some after the hike.
Great idea! We can also drink some sweet tea to make the spice feel better. Have you ever been to Jiuzhaigou?
No, I have never been there. Is it far from here?
It is quite far, about four hours by bus. But the water there is very blue and clear. If you have time next month, you should visit it. It is worth the trip.

messages.content: Hi, I'm Liu Fang. I retired last year from a school in Kunming. I love hiking in the Stone Forest. The trails are beautiful this time of year. What do you think about the mountain paths there?
Hello, Liu Fang! I'm a volunteer park ranger here. Actually, the stone pillars are amazing, but the dirt trails can be tricky if it rains. I've been guiding groups since last spring.
Yes, I've heard that. Do you bring enough water for the long walk? I usually carry two big bottles. Is that enough for a full day?

To be honest, two bottles might not be enough if you plan to climb the high peaks. The weather gets hot quickly, and you lose water fast. You should also bring some fresh watermelon to stay refreshed.
That's a good point. But speaking of your experience, I'm very curious about your life. Are you married? Do you have any children who live nearby in Kunming?
Well, I'm single now, but I grew up in Dali and moved to Kunming for work. Anyway, let's get back to hiking. Do you usually go with friends or do you like hiking alone?
I prefer going with friends, like my old colleagues. We often meet at the local tea house before we start. It makes the trip much more enjoyable.

That sounds lovely! Meeting at a tea house is a great idea. In fact, many locals do that. You might want to try drinking a cup of Pu'er tea before you leave. Have you ever seen any wild monkeys on the trail?
Oh yes, we saw a group of langurs near the top last week. They were very shy but curious. It was quite exciting to watch them in the trees.

Wow, that must have been special! I remember seeing one sitting on a rock last summer. Although they are shy, they are used to tourists now. If you see one, keep a safe distance, please. Is there anything else you want to pack for wildlife watching?
I guess a small binoculars would be helpful. Also, I should wear comfortable shoes. I bought new hiking boots last month from a local shop. They fit perfectly.
Perfect! Comfortable shoes are very important. I wear my old boots because they are waterproof. Speaking of packing, don't forget to bring a map of the park. You might get lost if you go too far.
Good advice. I usually check the map at the entrance gate. By the way, did you live in Beijing before you came to Yunnan? I know many people from the capital move here for the fresh air.
Actually, no, I was born in Chengdu and moved to Yunnan twenty years ago. I love the cool climate here. Anyway, are you planning to visit the Stone Forest again next month?
Yes, I definitely will. I want to try the sunrise hike next time. It's said that the view is the best at that time. What time does the gate open?
The gate opens at 6:00 AM in summer. You should arrive early to beat the crowds. If you want, I can show you the best spot for photos. It's a bit of a walk from the main road, but it's worth it.

Actually, I haven't been sleeping well. I've been working late at my office in Xuanwu Lake area, and I'm thinking about quitting my job if things don't improve. Do you think I should take a vacation?
Well, taking a break is a good idea, but let's focus on your health first. You mentioned you feel tired. Is it mostly in the afternoon, or all day?

No, my chest is fine. I just feel very sleepy after lunch. Maybe I should eat less rice and eat more vegetables instead.
That's a good thought. Eating more vegetables is healthy. I usually suggest a balanced diet with some soy milk for the breakfast. Do you drink tea often?
Yes, I drink jasmine tea every day. It helps me relax. But now I feel like I need to buy a new one because the old one is broken.
Oh, I see. Well, your tea is fine for drinking, but for now, let's talk about your prescription. If you have fatigue, I might suggest some vitamins. Do you want me to write it down?
Yes, please write it. Also, can you recommend a good pharmacy near the hospital so I can pick it up later?

Of course. You can go to the pharmacy in the same building, it's very convenient. Here is your prescription for Vitamin B complex. It should help with your energy levels since you've been working hard.
Thank you so much. I will take it as soon as I get home. I'm really grateful for your help today.

Yeah, I try to walk in the park near my home every day. But honestly, I feel very tired lately, especially after work. My back hurts a lot.

I tried ginger tea once. It was okay. But my main problem is that I do not have time to cook healthy meals. I usually just order takeout from restaurants near my office.

I work in the business district of Tianhe. The traffic is terrible there every day. It makes me very stressed. I guess I should try to find a different job closer to home.

Wow, that's great! Well, I'm Li, and I'm a vendor here in Yiwu Market. Oolong is my favorite too. Where do you buy your tea from usually?
I usually buy it at a small shop near my office in Shenzhen. But I've heard that tea markets here are better.
You're right. In fact, this market in Guangzhou has the best prices. By the way, do you know how to brew the water temperature for oolong? It's very important.
I think 90 degrees is fine. But I've noticed that people in my company often drink American coffee instead. It's strange because tea is healthier.

That is true, actually. But honestly, many people prefer coffee now because it gives them energy faster. Speaking of energy, how long have you been working as a businessman? I guess I've only been selling tea for three years.

I've been working for fifteen years since I graduated from university. What about you? Are you married? Do you have children? And where do you live exactly? I mean, do you like living in Guangzhou compared to Beijing?

Small ones are better for tasting the aroma. I often bring my own teapot when I travel.
That's a good habit. In addition, you should carry a thermos if you travel far. For example, I like to take Pu'er tea from Yunnan because it gets better with age.
Yes, Pu'er is very special. I tried it last year but it was too strong for me. What do you think about the new tea styles from Fujian?
I think Fujian tea is very popular now. Although some people say it's too sweet, I like the floral taste. Have you ever visited Wuyi Mountain to taste the rock tea personally?
No, I haven't. I'm planning to go there next month if I have the time. Do you think the train from Shenzhen is convenient?
Yes, the high-speed train is very fast. You can stop in Nanping to see the nature. It's much better than driving.

messages.content: Hi, I'm Hao. It's evening in Guangzhou, right? I just finished a busy day at the office and I really want to try some real tea. Do you know any good places to buy leaves here?

Hello, Hao. Yes, it's evening and the old tea market is very lively right now. Actually, there are so many shops selling different kinds of tea. I've been here since I opened my shop five years ago. Would you like to try some fresh Pu'er tea from Yunnan?

That sounds interesting. I've heard Pu'er is very old. But honestly, I think the real problem with modern life is that everyone is too busy to stop and appreciate small things like this. We just rush from work to work without thinking. What do you think, is life moving too fast?
That's a deep thought, I guess. Many people feel that way, especially after a hard day. Anyway, speaking of tea, do you prefer drinking it hot or cold in the spring weather here?
Hot, definitely. Cold tea is just for summer. Have you ever tried brewing it with a special clay pot? I heard it makes the flavor better.
Yes, I use a clay pot sometimes. It's great for keeping the heat in. Actually, the water temperature is very important for this. If the water is too hot, it can make the tea taste bitter.
Oh, I see. So I need to control the temperature carefully. My boss always tells me that details matter, but he doesn't know how to make tea. It's quite frustrating when people don't listen.
Hmm, that can be annoying. But maybe he learns something if he tries it himself. By the way, do you know how to store these tea leaves properly after you buy them?
I store them in a box at home. It's okay, but I'm not an expert. I think I should learn more about the history of tea in China. It would be fun to know more stories about famous tea traders.

That's a great idea! There are many stories about tea in Fuzhou and Hangzhou. For example, the famous merchants who traveled far and wide. Anyway, let's focus on the leaves here. Would you like to smell this sample of Tieguanyin?
Yes, please. The smell is amazing. It reminds me of my grandmother's kitchen. She used to make tea every morning.
That's very sweet. Many people miss their family's tea time. In addition, this Tieguanyin has a strong floral scent. Would you like to buy a small bag to try at home?
Yes, I will. The price is reasonable too. I think I'll bring some back to my parents in Chengdu.

messages.content: Hi Qiang Li! I'm Xiao Fang. I just bought an old apartment in Tang Paradise Community in Xi'an. It's in a historic district, so the building is very old. I want to renovate it, but I'm worried about the noise. There is construction nearby, and it's been going on for weeks.

Hello Xiao Fang! Well, that sounds exciting. Actually, I have many clients in Tang Paradise who face exactly the same problem. Construction noise is terrible, especially in the summer when everyone is sleeping late. Have you checked the safety standards of the new materials yet? You must make sure the old walls are stable before you start.

Yes, I checked the safety standards last week. The workers said the beams are strong enough. But now I am thinking about choosing new furniture. I saw a shop in Lantian District that sells very nice wooden chairs.

That's good to hear about the safety. Of course, furniture is the next big step. I guess wooden chairs are traditional and fit the old style of Tang Paradise perfectly. Do you like dark wood or light wood better? I know a few local workshops that make hand-carved tables.

I prefer dark wood because it looks more classic. But I am thinking of going to the Shaanxi History Museum this weekend to see the new exhibition on Tang dynasty pottery. It opened yesterday, and I really want to go there with my family.

Wow, that sounds like a great plan! Well, the museum exhibition must be very interesting, especially the Tang pottery. However, by the way, don't you have to deal with the furniture choice soon? The noise from the construction might stop soon, so you should decide the style before the workers come back.

You are right, but I need inspiration first. If I go to the museum, I can see how they used wood back then. Maybe I will buy some small items from there too. Anyway, what do you think about the wooden chairs?

That's a smart idea because the museum pieces are authentic. Actually, I think dark wood is a safe choice for a historic district. It matches the old bricks and tiles of your building in Xi'an very well. What about the size? Do you need large dining tables or small coffee tables?
I need a large dining table for my family dinners. We usually eat dumplings and hotpot on weekends. My husband loves hotpot, so I want a sturdy table. Can you recommend a brand that is reliable?

Ah, hotpot! That is delicious food in Shaanxi, especially with spicy broth. Yes, a sturdy table is essential for that. I know a brand called 'Century Wood' that makes very durable tables. They have a shop near the north gate of Xi'an. Would you like me to check their prices for you?
Yes, please check their prices. But first, I want to know if the noise will stop soon. The workers are drilling every day since Monday morning. It is very annoying.

I understand, drilling is very loud! To be honest, it depends on the construction schedule. Usually, the noisy work stops after three weeks. If the weather is too hot, they might take a break during the hottest part of the day. Have you asked the manager if they have a finish date?
No, I haven't asked yet. I will call them tomorrow. In the meantime, I am worried that the noise will damage the new furniture I buy. Do you think it is better to wait until the noise stops?

That's a valid concern. Actually, most furniture is not damaged by normal construction noise. As long as you don't put heavy items on the floor while they are drilling, it should be fine. You can buy the dark wood chairs now and keep them in the box until the noise stops.
That makes sense. I can keep the chairs in the box. But I still want to visit the museum to get ideas. What time does the exhibition close?

The Shaanxi History Museum usually closes at 5:30 PM on weekends. That gives you plenty of time to see the Tang dynasty pottery. By the way, why don't you bring some samples of your dark wood to compare? That way, you can see which pieces match best when you get back.

It's a dull pain at the back of my head. I feel very tired after work every day.

Actually, I've been feeling this way for months. It started right after I moved to Hangzhou from my hometown in Wenzhou.
Oh, moving can be really stressful. Well, let's focus on your symptoms first. Do you take any medicine now?

Yes, 9:00 is perfect. But honestly, I'm wondering if you ever get tired of answering these questions all day.

Great. I'll be there with my ID card.
Perfect. Please bring your ID card. We'll see you soon.

messages.content: Hello, I am Xiao Fang. I need to book a doctor's appointment because I have been feeling very tired since last week.
Hi Xiao Fang, welcome to our Hangzhou Community Health Center. I'm Li Wei. I'm sorry to hear you're feeling tired. Do you also have a headache or any other symptoms?
Yes, my head hurts a lot in the morning. Actually, I think the stress from work at the office in Yuhang District is making things worse. I haven't slept well since I started working late.

That makes sense, Xiao Fang. Work stress can definitely cause headaches and poor sleep. We have a good doctor here who specializes in stress and headaches. Would you like me to book you for tomorrow morning?

Okay, but to be honest, I don't really think physical health is the only problem. Many people today ignore their mental state and just keep working. We are too busy to rest, and that is why society is becoming so anxious. We should change our mindset about life instead of just taking medicine.

You have a point about mental health being important, and I agree that we all need to slow down sometimes. Anyway, let's focus on your appointment for now. Can you come to the clinic at 9:30 AM tomorrow?
Yes, 9:30 works for me. Do I need to bring anything special?
Well, you just need to bring your ID card and your health insurance card. We don't need anything else for the first visit. Do you have your insurance card with you today, or should we mail it to you?
I have my ID card, but I lost my insurance card last month. Can you help me find it or send a new one?

I can call our insurance department to check the status for you. It usually takes about one week to get a replacement card. While we are waiting, do you have any specific symptoms you want to tell the doctor about, like the headache or the tiredness?
Yes, the headache is the main thing. It feels like a tight band around my head. Also, I feel dizzy when I stand up quickly.

Those are important details to tell the doctor. A tight band feeling often means tension headaches. Okay, I will book you for 9:30 AM tomorrow with Dr. Chen. Is there anything else you need help with before you go?
